You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content: "63 :     public String get(final int i) {\n64 :         return values[i];\n65 :     }"

Title: Diagnosis

Details:
- Failing test intent:
  - testGetStringInconsistentRecord mutates the header map to include a key "fourth" mapped to index 4, then calls recordWithHeader.get("fourth"). It expects an IllegalArgumentException when the header mapping points past the number of values in the record.
- Relevant implementation:
  - CSVRecord constructor stores values and mapping without validation:
    - CSVRecord(String[] values, Map<String, Integer> mapping, String comment, long recordNumber)
      - Sets this.values and this.mapping directly (no size or consistency checks).
  - CSVRecord.get(String) performs only a null mapping check, then looks up the index and directly indexes into the values array:
    - public String get(final String name) {
        if (mapping == null) { throw new IllegalStateException(...); }
        final Integer index = mapping.get(name);
        return index != null ? values[index.intValue()] : null;
      }
    - There is no bounds check on index against values.length.
  - CSVRecord.get(int) also directly indexes values without bounds checks:
    - public String get(final int i) { return values[i]; }
- How the bug manifests:
  - In the test, the header map is made inconsistent with the record values by inserting "fourth" -> 4. If the record has fewer than 5 fields (values.length <= 4), then values[4] will throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException from the JVM array access.
  - The test expects an IllegalArgumentException to indicate an inconsistent header-to-values mapping; instead, the current implementation allows the out-of-range index to bubble up as an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
- Relation to the issue report:
  - The report states that CSVRecord does not verify that the header mapping size matches the number of values, leading to ArrayOutOfBoundsException when accessing a header beyond the available values (e.g., record.get("C") when header has A, B, C but the row has only a, b).
  - This is exactly what happens in get(String): no verification at construction time and no index range check at access time cause an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of a controlled IllegalArgumentException.
- Conclusion:
  - The failure occurs because CSVRecord.get(String) does not validate that the mapped column index is within the bounds of the values array. Combined with the constructor not validating header-to-values consistency, this leads to ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException rather than the expected IllegalArgumentException when the mapping is inconsistent with the record length.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

CSVRecord.get(java.lang.String)
CSVRecord.CSVRecord(java.lang.String[], java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Integer>, java.lang.String, long)
